newsitem.title: CANADA: North and Central America port conditions - Lloyds.
newsitem.headline: North and Central America port conditions - Lloyds.

text.p: Port conditions from Lloyds Shipping Intelligence Service --

CANADA, Nov 4 - Vancouver, B.C. - GRAIN - 4 Vessels loading, 10 waiting, 5-7 days waiting time expected depending on grade to be loaded. 20 Vessels due between 7 and 22/11. COAL - Roberts Bank - 2 Vessels loading, 19 due to load a total of 1,800,000 tonnes prior to the end of November. 15 Vessels/positions scheduled for December for a total of 1,200,000 tonnes. Prince Rupert - GRAIN - 1 Vessel loading, 4 waiting, 7-10 days delay expected waiting for cargo. November 5 -Halifax, N.S. - All terminals operating normally. Both container terminals advise no delays. Break-bulk piers have space available. Inner harbour anchorage clear and uncongested. Pier 9a closed for repairs which are expected to be completed summer 1997. Reconstruction of pier 26/27 expected to be complete January 1997 to include resurfacing and 65,000 sq. ft. Shed to specialise in forest products. Halifax shipyards and Dartmouth marine slips available for repairs.

HONDURAS, Nov 4 - Puerto Cortes - One vessel berthed discharging/loading containers, 1 anchored waiting to load bananas, 13 due of which 8 to discharge/load containers, 5 to load bananas. No berthing delays expected. Puerto Cortes - Six vessels berthed of which 3 discharging/loading containers, 1 loading bananas, 2 discharging general cargo, 3 awaiting berths of which 2 to discharge/load containers, 1 to load bananas/discharge containers. 16 Vessels due of which 6 to discharge/load containers, 4 to discharge/load general cargo, 4 to load bananas, 1 to discharge petroleum products, 1 to discharge industrial explosives.

MEXICO, Nov 5 - All ports working normally. Tampico - Eight vessels in port of which 3 minerals, 2 containers, 1 cement, 1 gasoline, 1 under repair. Veracruz - 14 In port of which 2 sugar, 2 pipes, 4 corn, 4 wheat, 2 general cargo. Manzanillo - Seven in port of which 1 cars, 2 general cargo, 1 fruit, 2 steel coils, 1 oil tanker. Coatzacoalcos - Sixteen vessels in port of which 7 chemicals, 8 oil tankers, 1 under repair.

PANAMA, Nov 4 - Balboa - One tanker, 1 general cargo vessel. Cristobal - One general cargo vessel, 2 container carriers, 1 ro/ro/container carer. Panama Canal - Working at full capacity 4/11. From 5/11-11/11 single lane outages at Miraflores and Gatun locks for maintenance and repairs. The number of bookings allocated will be reduced from 6/11 until further notice. Conditions 4/11 31 vessels due, 22 in queue, 11 booked, 33 scheduled. Conditions 3/11 actual arrivals 36, transits 37. Average of non-booked and booked canal waters time 18.0 hrs. Weather foggy, with heavy rain.

EL SALVADOR, Nov 1 - Acajutla - Three vessels discharging at berth (1 fertiliser, 1 tallow, 1 bulk wheat). 1 Vessel discharging diesel at anchor. 6 Vessels due 10/11 of which 4 to discharge (1 vehicles, 1 rice, 1 steel, 1 steel products). 1 To discharge full containers/load empty containers, 1 fuel oil. Delays depending on weather. Rainy season May-October.

UNITED STATES, Nov 5 - Jersey City, NJ - One vessel in port. Port Newark, NJ - Two vessels in port. Port Elizabeth - One vessel in port. Perth Amboy, Cartaret - No vessels in port. Bayway - Two vessels in port. All northern New Jersey ports working normally, with no congestion/delays. Baltimore, MD - Port working normally. Seven bulkers, 5 container vessels, 2 ro/ros, 1 auto vessel, 3 tankers, 3 general cargo vessels. 2 Cable vessels on stand-by, 3 vessels in repair yard. 4 Bulkers awaiting berths of which 1 to sail, 2 to discharge sugar/salt, 1 under arrest. Honolulu, Hi - Honolulu harbour - 4 Container vessels, 4 tugs/barges berthed, 1 vessel berthed for repairs. Honolulu anchorage - 1 Vessel anchored for bunkers. Barbers Point harbour - 2 Tugs/barges berthed. Nov 5 - Hampton Roads, VA - Six general cargo/container vessels berthed and operating, 2 bulkers berthed loading coal, 2 anchored waiting to load, 1 loading grain. 1 Tanker anchored lightering crude oil, 2 bulkers berthed discharging minerals.

East coast Baltimore, MD - No congestion at Dundalk terminal anticipated this week. C/D canal/Baltimore harbour low ceiling. Elevators and coal operations working well, no delays. Average waiting time at Consol coal 4 days. Liquid bulk facilities operating normally, no berthing congestion. Anchorage clear at Baltimore and Annapolis. Charleston, SC - Container terminals, north charleston and Wando Welch remain very busy. Charleston branch pilots announced new draft regulation for all vessels calling the Wando Welch and Columbus St. terminals. New regulation increases the draft from 37 ft to 38 ft for 24 hour pilotage. Any vessel with a deep draft greater than 38 ft will be required to move on a tidal window. Allied Terminal advises three vessels discharging petroleum products over the next week. No vessels due at present at grain elevator.

Jacksonville, FL - No heavy berthing congestion or delays for Jacksonville and Fernandina Beach. FL. Miami - Excellent berth availability for container, ro/ro and bulk vessels. Cruise ship terminals are full as usual from Friday through to Monday. New York, NY - No congestion at New York anchorages, none at container sugar, or tanker terminals. Norfolk, VA - Norfolk southern coal pier expecting 12 vessels this week. At present, 1 vessel anchored waiting to load. Dominion terminal expecting 9 vessels. Pier IX coal terminal expecting 5 vessels during week. Cargill not expecting any vessels in coming week. Container and general cargo terminals working normally, no delays. Oil and bulk terminals all working normally.

Philadelphia, PA - No port congestion in Philadelphia, Camden or Wilmington. No activity as far as dredging, repairs or navigational problems. Savannah, GA - No congestion expected at Georgia ports authorities Garden City terminals and Ocean terminals throughout week. All liquid bulk facilities operating normally, no berthing congestion expected. Colonial marine terminals (bulk clay) expect no delays this week. Weather seasonal. Due to afternoon thunder showers vessels with weather-sensitive cargo may expect some downtime. Some delays expected due to fog in the early morning hours. All navigational conditions remain normal.

Gulf Coast Houston, TX - No congestion at Houston city docks or Houston and Galveston grain elevators. However, congestion in some oil/chemical terminals. Houston ship channel closes almost every night due to fog and reopens at daybreak. Mobile, Al - No congestion expected this week. New Orleans, LA - Normal for periods of rain during summer seasons, causing cause delays in cargo operation, especially grain loading. Grain shipments normal for season. River stage at 4.8 feet, normal transit times expected. Bar pilots advise Saturday and Sunday draft for Mississippi river gulf outlet will be 30 ft. Present max permissible draft at S.W. Pass 47 ft fresh water for vessels under 100,000 dwt, 46 ft for vessels over 100,000 dwt. Some elevators not working at weekends due to slower than usual grain shipments.

West coast, Columbia river - Wheat cargoes for November are expected to increase. Large charters of soft white wheat are the most active commodity in November corn cargo movements. Corn cargo movements down. Currently 16 grain vessels in Columbia river district with 11 scheduled to arrive next week. Currently 6 vessels loading and l0 waiting. Average waiting period 3-6 days. Coos Bay, Or - Traffic in past week consisted of 2 lumber and 2 woodchip vessels. Channel dredging going forward with no delays in traffic. Honolulu, HI - Crowding at off port anchorage in Honolulu has been alleviated, no delays in coming week.

Long Beach, CA - Metropolitan (LB 212-214) moderate for November. At present delays of 1-2 days at anchor for waiting berth. Koch Carbon (lb-211) 1 vessel scheduled for November. Kaiser (la-49 ) moderate for November. (Coal/petcoke) delays of up to 1-2 days waiting berth expected. November looks moderate in the Los Angeles/Long Beach harbour for bulk cargoes.
